# XPath expression built from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/xpath-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-643](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/643.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in the text of an XPath expression (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta REST):
the expression given to `compile`, `evaluate` or `evaluateExpression` of a JAXP
`javax.xml.xpath.XPath`. The document or `InputSource` the expression is evaluated against, the
values of XPath variables, and encoded values are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Quotes and operators in the value change the query. A title such as `' or '1'='1` turns
`//book[title='...']` into a query that matches every book; in a login query
(`//user[name='...' and password='...']`) it matches any user, which bypasses the check, and other
values can reveal parts of the document the page never meant to show.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the name is concatenated into the expression.

```java
package com.example.directory;

import javax.xml.xpath.XPath;
import javax.xml.xpath.XPathExpressionException;
import javax.xml.xpath.XPathFactory;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.w3c.dom.Document;

@RestController
public class EmailController {
    private final XPath xpath = XPathFactory.newInstance().newXPath();
    private Document users;

    @GetMapping("/email")
    public String email(@RequestParam String name) throws XPathExpressionException {
        return xpath.evaluate("/users/user[@name='" + name + "']/email", users);
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the expression is constant and the name is the XPath variable `$name`.

```java
package com.example.directory;

import javax.xml.xpath.XPath;
import javax.xml.xpath.XPathExpressionException;
import javax.xml.xpath.XPathFactory;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.w3c.dom.Document;

@RestController
public class EmailController {
    private Document users;

    @GetMapping("/email")
    public String email(@RequestParam String name) throws XPathExpressionException {
        XPath xpath = XPathFactory.newInstance().newXPath();
        xpath.setXPathVariableResolver(variable -> "name".equals(variable.getLocalPart()) ? name : null);
        return xpath.evaluate("/users/user[@name=$name]/email", users);
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the expression constant and pass request values as XPath variables: write `$name` in the
  expression and return the value from an `XPathVariableResolver` set with
  `xpath.setXPathVariableResolver(...)` before the expression is compiled or evaluated.
- Or pick the expression or its parts from a fixed allow-list, or convert numbers with
  `Integer.parseInt` / `Long.parseLong`.
- Where neither fits, encode the value with ESAPI `encodeForXPath`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)
- `javax.xml.xpath`

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Only the JAXP `javax.xml.xpath` API is checked: the XPath methods of dom4j (`selectNodes`,
  `createXPath`), JDOM and Jaxen are not.
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), except a Spring `HttpEntity` or `RequestEntity` (the
  request body and headers); enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as request data.
- One method is analysed at a time and conditions are not evaluated: a helper that returns a
  constant, or a switch over a constant, still passes the request data on, and a wrapper class that
  reads the request is not a source. Allow-list lookups are recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of
  constants and as `valueOf` of an enum declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/java/xpath/xpath-injection.java`](../../../rules/java/xpath/xpath-injection.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/java/xpath/xpath-injection.yml`](../../../rules/java/xpath/xpath-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.2.
